data.content_ref: inline:The claim mandates that changing a single checklist item to 'Fail' should logically propagate to the final judgment regardless of the 'obvious' answer, but this is a reliability test only if the checklist's logic is perfectly calibrated to the objective outcome. Counterexample: if the checklist item is a proxy indicator that can be false-positive (e.g., a symptom that is necessary in most but not all cases of the objectively verifiable condition), then a panel that blindly propagates the single 'Fail' to reject an actually-correct outcome is following a miscalibrated rule, not demonstrating reliability. Genuine reliability for objectively verifiable outcomes cannot require overriding the verifiable outcome whenever any one proxy item fails.
